title: Conduction, convection, radiation
examples: What is the difference between conduction and convection?
How does a vacuum flask keep things hot?
Can you give an example of heat transfer in daily life?

explain.say: Heat moves in three main ways through materials.

draw.text: 3 ways heat moves: conduction, convection, radiation

explain.say: Conduction is when heat moves by touching things together.
Convection happens when fluids move from hot to cool areas.
Radiation transfers heat using invisible waves, needing no medium.
Insulation uses materials to slow down heat transfer by all three ways.
A vacuum flask uses a vacuum and insulation to stop heat loss.

faq.q: Does heat always move from hot to cold?
faq.a: Yes, heat naturally flows from a warmer area to a cooler area. This is the direction of heat transfer.
asks: What is the direction of heat flow?

faq.q: Can radiation travel through a vacuum?
faq.a: Yes, radiation can travel through a vacuum, like the space between the Earth and the Sun. This is why we get solar energy.
asks: Does radiation need air to travel?
How does the sun heat Earth without air?

faq.q: Why do we use fluffy materials for insulation?
faq.a: Fluffy materials trap pockets of air, and air is a poor conductor of heat. This reduces heat loss effectively.
asks: Why is trapped air good for insulation?

faq.q: What is the main job of the vacuum space in a flask?
faq.a: The vacuum space removes the medium through which heat can transfer by conduction or convection. This greatly slows heat escape.
asks: Why is a vacuum useful for keeping things hot?
What stops heat loss in a vacuum flask?

faq.a: Neither is necessarily faster; it depends on the materials and setup. Both are forms of heat transfer through matter.
asks: Which heat transfer method is quickest?
Do conduction and convection have different speeds?

facts: Conduction occurs when particles vibrate and transfer energy.
Convection currents are responsible for weather patterns on Earth.
Radiation does not require any matter to travel.
A vacuum means there are almost no particles present.

quiz.say: When steam rises from a kettle, what process is happening?
quiz.why: Convection happens when hot fluids, like steam, become less dense and rise.

wrong.0: Conduction requires direct contact between solid objects.
wrong.1: Radiation uses waves and does not need a fluid medium.
wrong.2: Insulation is a material property, not a transfer method.

quiz.say: Which heat transfer method relies on invisible waves?
quiz.why: Radiation transfers energy using electromagnetic waves, like light or heat waves.

wrong.0: Conduction must pass through physical contact.
wrong.1: Convection needs a fluid, like air or water, to move.
wrong.2: A vacuum is the absence of matter, not the transfer method itself.

quiz.say: To stop heat loss from a drink, you should use:
quiz.why: A vacuum flask minimizes conduction, convection, and radiation loss using a vacuum.

wrong.0: Metal is a good conductor, so heat escapes quickly.
wrong.1: Open containers allow heat to escape by all three methods.
wrong.2: Adding liquid coolant would actually help heat escape.
